h: Blackpool's Long Love Affair With Ice
p: Blackpool has been dazzling visitors with ice entertainment for a very long time. Ice shows have been part of the resort's summer season for decades, with skaters, glittering costumes and big production numbers drawing in holidaymakers who fancied something more spectacular than a sing-along at the end of the pier. The resort's heritage of variety and showbusiness, from the Tower Circus to the Winter Gardens, means a slick, glamorous ice show feels right at home here.

If you do get the chance to skate, a few basics will make your first few minutes much less wobbly. Bend your knees slightly, keep your weight forward, and take small steps to begin with rather than trying to glide straight away. When you do lose your balance, and you will, try to bend your knees and drop to the side rather than falling backwards. Gloves help protect your hands, and thick socks stop hired skates rubbing.
Kids often pick it up far quicker than grown-ups because they're closer to the ground and less worried about looking daft. Let them show you how it's done.

Because the arena is indoors, it works well as an all-weather activity. Pair a show or skating session with an afternoon at the Pleasure Beach, a walk along South Pier or an evening tram ride along the prom. If you're visiting in the autumn, the Blackpool Illuminations add a magical glow to the seafront, stretching for miles and drawing visitors from all over the country. Ice and lights together make a cracking autumn break.
